tasks.prompt: To make an Envoy sidecar less likely to be OOM-killed, kubelet gives it an OOM score adjustment lower than the regular containers in the same Pod. Is that consistent with the design?
tasks.author: ai-task-writer-j

tasks.prompt: Explain in a few sentences what happens to sidecar containers when a Pod with sidecars terminates, including what is and is not guaranteed.

rubric.text: Sidecar PreStop hooks run when the Pod begins terminating, at the same time as those of regular containers, and this starts the grace period countdown.
Only after the last primary container terminates do sidecars get SIGTERM, one at a time in reverse start order.
If the grace period expires first, all remaining containers get SIGTERM, then a fixed 2s, then are killed.
Ordering and graceful termination are only guaranteed if the PreStop hook completes within the Pod's termination grace period.
Sidecars keep being restarted until they enter the Terminated state after their SIGTERM.

tasks.author: ai-task-writer-j

tasks.prompt: Summarise how an operator should safely roll back or downgrade the sidecar containers feature in a cluster that already runs Pods with sidecars.

rubric.text: Disable the feature gate on the control plane first, then on the nodes.
Disabling the gate on a node requires a kubelet restart.
Pods that had sidecars must be deleted and recreated without them.
A version downgrade requires draining the node.
A high kubelet_started_containers_errors_total count (init_container type) is the metric signalling a problem that should inform a rollback.

tasks.author: ai-task-writer-j
tasks.notes: cross-section: Upgrade/Downgrade Strategy and the Production Readiness questionnaire.

tasks.prompt: Summarise which lifecycle hooks and probes sidecar containers support compared with other init containers, and what sidecars are not meant to guarantee.

rubric.text: Sidecars support PostStart and PreStop handlers and startup, readiness and liveness probes; other init containers are not allowed them.
Sidecar readiness probes count toward the Pod's readiness.
The next init container starts once the sidecar's startup probe succeeded (or none is defined) and its postStart handler completed.
Sidecars are not a security control: their restart is best effort, so other containers are not guaranteed to run only while the sidecar is healthy.
